Best regards,

result.result:
The port agency's berth is firm — "the terminal has confirmed KESTREL MOOR's berth for 29 Jan 1200 UTC" — and it is about two days after the voyage system's current Qingdao ETA of 27 Jan 00:00 UTC. With the route clear (no avoid passages) and the berth well beyond the charter party's 12‑hour ETA‑change limit, slowing down is worth it: the voyage optimisation service's simulated speed advice says 7.4 kn would get the ship to Qingdao by 29 Jan 10:07 UTC, saving an estimated 58 hours at anchor and 109.4 t of VLSFO. The speed plan checks out (arrival before the berth, figures consistent), and an ETA notice is now due — the ETA has moved 58.1 hours since the last notice against a 12‑hour limit — to the agent and receiver.

The operator should decide whether to order the reduced speed. On a yes: (a) a speed instruction to the Master with the advised speed (7.4 kn) and arrival (29 Jan 10:07 UTC), noting that his judgement on the ship's safety in the weather ahead comes first; (b) the ETA notice due under check_notices, to the agent and receiver, with the new ETA of 29 Jan 10:07 UTC; and (c) a voyage management system entry for the Qingdao port call ETA. All figures from the speed advice are the voyage optimisation service's simulated figures. Recommend nothing be sent until the operator answers.
